title: Calling the Brane Next Door: The Kaluza-Klein Tower as a Gravitational Information Channel
summary: Could two worlds localised on neighbouring branes communicate through gravity alone? We investigate this question in a minimal higher-dimensional framework in which Standard Model fields are confined to our brane while gravity propagates through the bulk. From the brane-to-brane graviton propagator we derive the retarded transfer kernel of the inter-brane link and identify the transition from evanescent to propagating Kaluza-Klein modes. The central idea is to give the Kaluza-Klein tower a new role: not only as a spectrum of massive gravitational states, but as a set of communication carriers. Below the first KK threshold the channel is effectively four-dimensional and is mediated only by the massless graviton. Above threshold, massive KK modes open as additional propagating subchannels, and information may be encoded in their occupation pattern, relative phases, and arrival-time structure as well as in ordinary signal variables. The compactification determines the KK masses, wavefunctions, brane overlap factors, and propagation phases, which together define a multi-input multi-output (MIMO) channel matrix. In the resolved-mode limit, the tower yields approximate parallel subchannels, to which standard information-theoretic notions such as capacity bounds, water-filling, effective rank, and sparse occupancy codes apply. The production and detection of such signals are highly model-dependent and not assumed to be feasible with known technology. Nevertheless, the channel structure is well defined: a neighbouring brane-world could be separated from us by a microscopic distance in the compact space while remaining hidden because the only shared interaction is gravity. The first observable signature may not be a deliberate message, but the spectral and modal structure of the Kaluza-Klein tower itself, revealing partial information about the geometry of a nearby hidden world.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how two brane-worlds separated in a compact extra dimension could communicate via gravity alone, treating the Kaluza-Klein (KK) tower as a MIMO communication channel. Below the first KK threshold, only the massless graviton mediates; above threshold, massive KK modes act as propagating subchannels with distinct phases, wavefunctions, and brane overlaps. The compactification geometry defines a channel matrix whose properties (capacity, effective rank, water-filling) can be analysed information-theoretically. While practical detection is not assumed feasible, the first observable signature may be the spectral/modal structure of the KK tower itself, revealing the hidden world's geometry.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether two neighbouring brane-worlds can communicate through gravity alone, and to reframe the Kaluza-Klein tower not merely as a spectrum of massive gravitons but as a structured communication channel with information-theoretic properties.
AI.method: The authors compute the brane-to-brane graviton propagator to derive the retarded transfer kernel, identify the evanescent-to-propagating transition at the first KK threshold, and construct a MIMO channel matrix from the KK mode masses, wavefunctions, brane overlap factors, and propagation phases. Standard MIMO information-theoretic tools (capacity bounds, water-filling, effective rank, sparse codes) are then applied in the resolved-mode limit.
AI.result: Below the first KK threshold, the inter-brane channel is 4D and mediated only by the massless graviton. Above threshold, massive KK modes open as additional propagating subchannels, enabling information encoding in occupation patterns, relative phases, and arrival-time structure. The channel structure is well-defined even if detection is not feasible with known technology.
AI.conclusion: A neighbouring brane-world could be separated by a microscopic compact distance yet remain hidden because gravity is the only shared interaction. The first observable signature may be the spectral and modal structure of the KK tower itself, indirectly revealing the geometry of a nearby hidden world, rather than a deliberate message.

title: Maximal Transcendentality of the Double-Scaled PCM
summary: We prove, to all orders, maximal transcendentality of the strongly coupled large-N Principal Chiral Model in the double-scaling regime introduced in our earlier work. We also prove that, after a natural shift of the coupling constant, the coefficients of the vacuum-energy expansion are expressed purely as polynomials in odd zeta values with rational coefficients. The first 35 explicitly computed orders reveal further number-theoretic regularities, pointing to hidden structure beyond maximal transcendentality.

AI.tldr: The paper proves that the strongly coupled large-N Principal Chiral Model exhibits maximal transcendentality to all orders in the double-scaling regime, and that after shifting the coupling constant, the vacuum-energy expansion coefficients are pure polynomials in odd zeta values with rational coefficients. Explicit computations up to 35 orders reveal additional number-theoretic regularities suggesting hidden structure.
AI.motivation: To uncover hidden number-theoretic structures in the vacuum-energy expansion of the Principal Chiral Model beyond known maximal transcendentality properties.
AI.method: Analytic proof to all orders of maximal transcendentality in the double-scaling regime, combined with explicit computation of the first 35 orders of the vacuum-energy expansion after a natural shift of the coupling constant.
AI.result: Maximal transcendentality holds to all orders; after a shift of the coupling constant, the expansion coefficients are polynomials in odd zeta values with rational coefficients; the first 35 orders exhibit further regularities beyond maximal transcendentality.
AI.conclusion: The results confirm and extend the transcendentality properties of the model, and the additional regularities point toward yet deeper number-theoretic structures awaiting discovery.

title: Zeta Functions and the Superstring
summary: The superstring amplitude's Mellin transform in energy is computed at fixed momentum transfer. In the forward limit, it is shown that this transformed amplitude reduces to the Riemann zeta function, while for $t\neq 0$ it represents a deformation of $ζ$. This object exhibits remarkable mathematical properties as a result of physical attributes of the string amplitude. For integer subtractions, the dispersion relation defined by the Mellin transform yields the effective field theory expansion of the string amplitude order by order in $s$ at finite $t$, for which a new closed-form expression is derived.

AI.tldr: The Mellin transform of the superstring amplitude in energy at fixed momentum transfer yields the Riemann zeta function in the forward limit and a deformed zeta for non-zero t, leading to a closed-form dispersion relation that recovers the EFT expansion.
AI.motivation: To connect string theory amplitudes to number-theoretic objects (Riemann zeta function) and derive analytic properties that bridge high-energy physics and effective field theory.
AI.method: Computes the Mellin transform of the superstring amplitude at fixed t, analyzes the forward limit (t=0) and non-forward case, and uses dispersion relations with integer subtractions to recover the EFT expansion.
AI.result: The Mellin-transformed amplitude reduces to the Riemann zeta function in the forward limit and a deformation thereof for t≠0. A new closed-form expression for the dispersion relation yields the EFT expansion order by order in s at finite t.
AI.conclusion: The Mellin transform of the superstring amplitude reveals deep connections between string theory, zeta functions, and effective field theory, providing a novel closed-form expression for the EFT expansion.

title: Resonance and Differential Reduction of Feynman Integrals
summary: Feynman integrals may be viewed as generalized hypergeometric functions, and specifically as solutions of GKZ systems of partial differential equations that typically exhibit resonance. Resonance is a type of non-genericity implying reducibility to subsystems. We use this resonance to construct reduction operators, which are differential operators that can contract edges of Feynman graphs. Correspondingly, their action is naturally compatible with cuts of Feynman graphs. Reduction operators may be used to close the system of differential equations for a given integral. The remaining GKZ data lead to algebraic relations identifying a smaller system that is fully reduced to master integrals. We develop the construction for one-loop, sunrise and banana graphs and discuss restrictions to physical kinematics. While reduction operators can generally shift both propagator powers and spacetime dimension, certain combinations isolate a pure dimension shift together with contraction of a chosen edge.

AI.tldr: Feynman integrals are treated as GKZ hypergeometric functions exhibiting resonance, which enables construction of reduction operators that contract graph edges, close differential equation systems, and isolate master integrals.
AI.motivation: To develop a systematic method for reducing Feynman integrals to master integrals using the resonant structure of their GKZ systems, leveraging the natural compatibility with graph cuts.
AI.method: Resonance in GKZ systems is exploited to construct reduction operators—differential operators that contract edges of Feynman graphs. The construction is developed explicitly for one-loop, sunrise, and banana graphs, with analysis of physical kinematics restrictions.
AI.result: Reduction operators can close the system of differential equations for a given Feynman integral and the remaining GKZ data identifies a smaller system fully reduced to master integrals. Certain operator combinations isolate pure dimension shifts while contracting a chosen edge.
AI.conclusion: The GKZ/resonance framework provides a systematic algebraic approach to Feynman integral reduction, with natural compatibility between reduction operators and graph cuts.

title: Testing Supersymmetric Hidden Sectors with Long-Baseline Atom Interferometers
summary: Atomic interferometry provides a sensitive near Earth probe of high energy physics through precision measurements of quantum phase. In this Letter, we point out that MAGIS and AION like long-baseline atom interferometers can also be used to test supersymmetric hidden sectors, if these sectors contain ultralight moduli, dilatons or hidden scalars that induce coherent phase oscillations. In such a setup, the measured atomic phase does not only constrain an effective phenomenological scalar coupling. It can be related to derivatives of supersymmetric gauge kinetic functions, Kähler metrics, Yukawa couplings, Higgs sector parameters and the QCD scale along light hidden sector directions. We derive the mapping from a generic SUSY/SUGRA modulus to the effective atom interferometric coupling, and show that future phase sensitivities may probe very small visible sector admixtures of otherwise hidden fields. This identifies MAGIS/AION type experiments as non-collider probes of supersymmetric and string-motivated infrared relics, complementary to gravitational wave, astrophysical and collider searches.

AI.tldr: Long-baseline atom interferometers (MAGIS/AION) can probe supersymmetric hidden sectors by detecting phase oscillations from ultralight scalars (moduli, dilatons), with future sensitivity to tiny visible-sector admixtures, complementing collider, GW, and astrophysical searches.
AI.motivation: To extend the use of precision atom interferometry beyond conventional tests of high-energy physics to directly probe supersymmetric hidden sectors containing ultralight scalars, which are difficult to detect at colliders.
AI.method: Derives a mapping from generic SUSY/SUGRA moduli to effective atom-interferometric coupling, relating measured atomic phase to derivatives of gauge kinetic functions, Kähler metrics, Yukawa couplings, Higgs parameters, and the QCD scale along hidden sector directions.
AI.result: Future MAGIS/AION phase sensitivities may probe very small visible-sector admixtures of hidden fields, enabling detection of supersymmetric infrared relics.
AI.conclusion: MAGIS/AION-type experiments serve as non-collider probes of supersymmetric and string-motivated infrared relics, complementary to gravitational wave, astrophysical, and collider searches.

title: Where is tree-level heterotic string theory?
summary: We continue the tree-level S-matrix bootstrap program for quantum gravity, now in ten-dimensional theories with half-maximal supersymmetry. This setting includes the heterotic string and allows us to test whether the string-like structures found in the maximally supersymmetric bootstrap persist with less supersymmetry and in non-planar gauge sectors. Imposing analyticity, crossing symmetry, unitarity, and Regge boundedness, we constraint weakly coupled UV completions of supergravity and super Yang-Mills. In the gravitational sector, much of the boundary of the allowed region is explained by extremal amplitudes supported on a single linear Regge trajectory, or by convex combinations of such amplitudes. In the gluon sector, the non-planar problem reveals a tension between representation-channel positivity and the trace decomposition of the EFT data, obstructing a direct normalization by $G$ or $g_{\rm YM}$; a coupled gluon/graviton bootstrap may be necessary to directly constrain the relative strength of gauge and gravitational interactions. Overall, our results support the emergence of linear Regge trajectories as a robust feature of the tree-level quantum-gravity bootstrap.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the tree-level S-matrix bootstrap to 10D theories with half-maximal supersymmetry (including the heterotic string), finding that linear Regge trajectories emerge robustly in the gravitational sector, while the gluon sector faces normalization challenges that may require a coupled gluon/graviton bootstrap.
AI.motivation: To test whether the string-like structures found in the maximally supersymmetric bootstrap persist with less supersymmetry and in non-planar gauge sectors, using the heterotic string as a key example.
AI.method: Analyticity, crossing symmetry, unitarity, and Regge boundedness are imposed to constrain weakly coupled UV completions of supergravity and super Yang-Mills in 10D with half-maximal supersymmetry. Both gravitational and gluon sectors are analyzed, including non-planar contributions.
AI.result: The gravitational sector's allowed region is largely explained by extremal amplitudes on a single linear Regge trajectory or convex combinations thereof. The gluon sector's non-planar problem reveals a tension between representation-channel positivity and trace decomposition of EFT data, hindering direct normalization by G or g_YM.
AI.conclusion: Linear Regge trajectories are a robust feature of the tree-level quantum-gravity bootstrap. A coupled gluon/graviton bootstrap may be necessary to directly constrain the relative strength of gauge and gravitational interactions.

title: Radio Emission from High-Frequency Gravitational Wave Point Sources
summary: High-frequency gravitational waves (HFGWs) in the MHz to GHz regime can convert into radio photons in the presence of astrophysical magnetic fields through the inverse Gertsenshtein effect. We show that existing radio telescopes like CHIME and FAST are excellent tools for detecting HFGW sources, significantly outperforming many existing experiments at detecting primordial black hole (PBH) mergers, the most realistic sources of transient HFGWs. Radio telescopes are also uniquely sensitive to sources of monochromatic HFGW emission, such as ultralight boson clouds formed through superradiance around PBHs, and are likely to have excellent sensitivity to generic sources of detectable HFGWs.

AI.tldr: High-frequency gravitational waves (MHz-GHz) can convert into radio photons via the inverse Gertsenshtein effect in astrophysical magnetic fields. Existing radio telescopes like CHIME and FAST can detect these signals, outperforming many current experiments, especially for primordial black hole mergers, ultralight boson clouds, and other generic HFGW sources.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that existing radio telescopes are excellent and previously underappreciated tools for detecting high-frequency gravitational waves via the inverse Gertsenshtein effect, particularly for transient sources like primordial black hole mergers and monochromatic sources like ultralight boson clouds.
AI.method: The authors analyze the conversion of HFGWs into radio photons in astrophysical magnetic fields (inverse Gertsenshtein effect), and evaluate the sensitivity of existing radio telescopes (CHIME, FAST) compared to other experiments for detecting various HFGW sources.
AI.result: Radio telescopes like CHIME and FAST significantly outperform many existing experiments for detecting primordial black hole mergers, are uniquely sensitive to monochromatic HFGW sources (e.g., ultralight boson clouds), and have excellent sensitivity to generic detectable HFGW sources.
AI.conclusion: Existing radio telescopes are powerful and versatile detectors for high-frequency gravitational waves, offering a new observational window for astrophysics and fundamental physics.

title: Testing F-theory GUTs with the Axiverse
summary: We show that axions coupled to photons in F-theory Grand Unified Theories (GUTs) satisfy the coupling-to-mass relation $g_{aγ}/m_a \leq C\, \frac{α_{\rm em}}{2π}\frac{1}{m_πf_π}$, with $C$ a calculable coefficient. This bound is saturated for the QCD axion with $C = \mathcal{O}(1)$ and holds in field theoretic and perturbative heterotic GUT constructions. In F-theory, topological GUT symmetry breaking by hypercharge flux introduces axion-like particles (ALPs) coupled to photons without coupling to QCD. These ALPs arise from the non-universal holomorphic threshold corrections to the gauge kinetic functions induced by the hypercharge flux. When gauge couplings approximately unify near the string scale, as required in phenomenologically viable models, the shift symmetries of these ALPs are broken by D-instantons whose action is controlled by the size of the threshold corrections to the gauge couplings. Small corrections imply unsuppressed instantons and heavy ALPs. We compute the resulting axion potentials and show that the coupling-to-mass ratio $g_{aγ}/m_a$ for every non-universal ALP lies well below the QCD axion prediction. We consider possible loopholes to this result -- some of which could lead to $C\gg 1$ -- and argue that none of them allows for $g_{aγ}/m_a$ to be arbitrarily above the QCD axion prediction within regions of control for the effective action. The bound persists in models with large threshold corrections, where new incomplete GUT multiplets at intermediate energy scales are required. As a result, in the geometric regime, where the $α'$ expansion is under control, no ALP parametrically above the QCD axion band exists. Our results make F-theory GUTs falsifiable: finding an ALP far above the QCD band, for example discovering axion-induced cosmic birefringence, rules out F-theory GUTs in regimes of control of the effective theory.

AI.tldr: F-theory GUTs predict a bound on the coupling-to-mass ratio of axions coupled to photons, which is saturated by the QCD axion but cannot be parametrically exceeded by ALPs in controlled regimes, making these models falsifiable by ALP detection above the QCD band.
AI.motivation: To determine whether axion-like particles (ALPs) in F-theory GUTs can achieve coupling-to-mass ratios significantly above the QCD axion prediction, and to establish falsifiable predictions for these string-theoretic constructions.
AI.method: The authors analyze the coupling-to-mass relation for axions coupled to photons in F-theory GUTs, studying non-universal holomorphic threshold corrections from hypercharge flux, D-instanton effects that break ALP shift symmetries, and the resulting axion potentials. They consider loopholes like large threshold corrections and intermediate-scale GUT multiplets.
AI.result: Every non-universal ALP in F-theory GUTs has a coupling-to-mass ratio well below the QCD axion prediction. The bound g_{aγ}/m_a ≤ C (α_em/2π)(1/(m_π f_π)) holds, with C = O(1) for the QCD axion. No ALP parametrically above the QCD axion band exists in the geometric regime.
AI.conclusion: F-theory GUTs are falsifiable: discovering an ALP far above the QCD axion band (e.g., via cosmic birefringence) would rule out F-theory GUTs in controlled regimes of the effective theory.

title: Too Heavy to Hide: Gamma-Ray Constraints on Annihilating Dark Matter beyond Unitarity
comment: v1: 18 pages, 4 figures. Comments are welcome. For a short video explaining the paper, please see: https://youtu.be/xsLzPSUIAD0?si=oZIvHp5FQueRHw6J
summary: The measurement of high energy diffuse gamma rays by various ground-based air shower detectors have opened a new chapter for high energy particle physics and astrophysics. The broad range of viable dark matter candidates motivates extending indirect searches to heavier dark matter masses, opening new opportunities to uncover the nature of dark matter. If dark matter is composite rather than point-like, then the thermal unitarity bound can be relaxed, opening up the possibility of dark matter masses far beyond the electroweak scale. We perform a model agnostic search for heavy annihilating dark matter using the gamma-ray measurements and upper limits from Tibet AS$_γ$, LHAASO, KASCADE-Grande, Pierre Auger Observatory, and Telescope Array. These highest energy datasets enable us to probe new regions of parameter space and set world-leading limits on the annihilation cross sections for dark matter masses $10^5$--$10^{12}$ GeV. Our work highlights the power of high energy gamma-ray datasets in discovering heavy dark matter signatures in the near future.

AI.tldr: Using gamma-ray data from Tibet ASγ, LHAASO, KASCADE-Grande, Pierre Auger Observatory, and Telescope Array, this paper performs a model-agnostic search for heavy annihilating dark matter (10⁵–10¹² GeV), setting world-leading limits on annihilation cross sections and demonstrating the potential of high-energy gamma-ray detectors to probe composite dark matter beyond the electroweak scale.
AI.motivation: The broad range of viable dark matter candidates motivates extending indirect searches to heavier dark matter masses. Composite dark matter can evade the thermal unitarity bound, allowing masses far beyond the electroweak scale, yet this high-mass regime remains largely unexplored.
AI.method: A model-agnostic search is performed using gamma-ray measurements and upper limits from five major air shower detectors: Tibet ASγ, LHAASO, KASCADE-Grande, Pierre Auger Observatory, and Telescope Array.
AI.result: World-leading limits on annihilation cross sections for dark matter masses in the range 10⁵–10¹² GeV are set, probing new regions of parameter space.
AI.conclusion: High-energy gamma-ray datasets are powerful tools for discovering heavy dark matter signatures, and the results highlight the potential for near-future detection.

title: Anomaly-driven evaporation endpoints of a two-dimensional regular black hole
summary: Spherical reduction of four-dimensional minimally coupled matter yields a two-dimensional theory with dilaton-coupled matter rather than minimally coupled conformal matter. We use this distinction to revisit the backreacted late-time endpoint problem for the regular two-dimensional Bardeen-like black hole considered by Barenboim, Frolov, and Kunstatter. Replacing the Polyakov quantum sector by the dilaton-coupled anomaly model of Fabbri, Farese, and Navarro-Salas (FFN), we derive the corresponding semiclassical field equations and classify the asymptotically allowed late branches at finite radius. For any quiescent finite-radius branch with finite nonzero conformal factor, the late-time mixed equation enforces $J'(r_\infty)=0$, and hence $r_\infty=\sqrt{2}\,\ell$, independently of the local dilaton-anomaly convention. For finite-radius null branches satisfying the stated state-tail assumptions, the ordinary strong-cosmic-censorship-restoring exponential null boundary is excluded. Generic power-law branches $e^{2ρ}\sim v^{-p}$ with $p>1$ are likewise excluded, except for the borderline case $p=2$, which is the only remaining null loophole of this type. In the FFN model, the settled realization of this loophole carries finite affine flux and requires the stronger state-tail decay $s_φ=O(v^{-2})$. The natural finite-radius outcome is remnant-like, while the surviving null branch is a highly constrained soft-null alternative.

AI.tldr: The paper studies the late-time endpoint of a 2D Bardeen-like black hole using dilaton-coupled matter (FFN model) instead of standard conformal matter. It finds that finite-radius branches force a specific radius \(r_\infty=\sqrt{2}\,\ell\), excludes exponential null boundaries and generic power-law branches except the borderline \(p=2\) case, which is the only remaining null loophole, leading to either a remnant-like outcome or a highly constrained soft-null alternative.
AI.motivation: To revisit the backreacted late-time endpoint problem for a regular 2D Bardeen-like black hole by properly accounting for the fact that spherical reduction of 4D minimally coupled matter yields dilaton-coupled matter, not minimally coupled conformal matter, and to classify the asymptotically allowed late-time branches.
AI.method: The authors replace the Polyakov quantum sector with the dilaton-coupled anomaly model of Fabbri, Farese, and Navarro-Salas (FFN), derive the semiclassical field equations, and classify asymptotically allowed late branches at finite radius through analytic analysis of the mixed equations and state-tail decay conditions.
AI.result: For quiescent finite-radius branches, \(J'(r_\infty)=0\) and \(r_\infty=\sqrt{2}\,\ell\) independently of the dilaton-anomaly convention. Exponential null boundaries are excluded. Generic power-law branches \(e^{2\rho}\sim v^{-p}\) with \(p>1\) are excluded except \(p=2\), which remains the only null loophole. In the FFN model, this loophole requires stronger state-tail decay \(s_\phi=O(v^{-2})\) and carries finite affine flux.
AI.conclusion: The natural finite-radius outcome is remnant-like, while the surviving null branch is a highly constrained soft-null alternative, offering a new classification of late-time black hole endpoints in dilaton-coupled semiclassical gravity.

title: Probing lepton number violation at FCC-ee
summary: We propose high-multiplicity final-state signatures, such as $e^+e^-\to N\overline{N}\to \ell^+\ell^+ 4j$ with $\ell$ denoting $e,~μ$, $τ$, as probes of lepton number violation (LNV) at FCC-ee, featuring negligible Standard Model background. In contrast to conventional searches such as $pp\to \ell^+ N \to \ell^+ \ell^+ jj$ or the process $e^+e^-\toνN$, which are suppressed by the small neutrino masses in conventional seesaw scenarios, the minimal linear seesaw picture avoids this suppression. This enables a direct LNV probe from final-state topology, with over $\mathcal{O}(10^3)$ events expected at FCC-ee. Besides probing the Majorana nature of neutrinos, this offers a novel avenue to test the neutrino mass ordering established by oscillation experiments in a high-energy collider setting.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using high-multiplicity final-state signatures (e+e− → N\N → ℓ+ℓ+4j) to probe lepton number violation at FCC-ee, avoiding suppression from small neutrino masses in seesaw scenarios, with O(10³) expected events and negligible SM background.
AI.motivation: Conventional LNV searches (e.g., pp → ℓ+N → ℓ+ℓ+jj or e+e− → νN) are suppressed by small neutrino masses in standard seesaw scenarios. The authors aim to find a more sensitive probe of lepton number violation and the Majorana nature of neutrinos at future colliders.
AI.method: The authors propose the process e+e− → N\N → ℓ+ℓ+4j (ℓ = e, μ, τ) in the minimal linear seesaw framework, which avoids the suppression from tiny neutrino masses. They analyze the final-state topology as a direct LNV signature at FCC-ee with negligible Standard Model background.
AI.result: Over O(10³) signal events are expected at FCC-ee with negligible SM background. The minimal linear seesaw scenario avoids the suppression that plagues conventional seesaw-based searches, enabling a detectable LNV signature.
AI.conclusion: This approach provides a direct LNV probe at FCC-ee, testing the Majorana nature of neutrinos, and offers a novel collider-based method to probe the neutrino mass ordering established by oscillation experiments.

title: Bootstrap Cone of the Multicritical Deconfined Quantum Critical Point
summary: The deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) provides a prominent example of the unconventional phase transitions beyond the Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson paradigm and its nature has been controversial for decades. The DQCP has been extensively studied and the results lead to two opposite scenarios with pseudo-criticality or multicriticality. The pseudo-criticality is a prevailing scenario of DQCP which interprets the approximately scale invariant numerical results with the walking behavior near complex fixed points. In contrast, the multicriticality scenario conjectures the DQCP is a unitary fixed point with a relevant $SO(5)$ singlet scalar. In this work we provide substantial evidence for the multicriticality scenario using conformal bootstrap. We start with the observation that the large scale Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) results nearly saturate the bootstrap bounds. After imposing suitable sparseness condition the bootstrap bound forms a sharp cone in the three-dimensional parameter space. The bootstrap cone is close to the QMC data. We use the navigator algorithm to locate the apex of the cone and extract the extremal solutions. We find striking consistencies between the bootstrap solutions and the fuzzy sphere data of DQCP, including the coefficients in the operator product expansions (OPEs) and the higher spectrum! The bootstrap cone unifies the QMC and the fuzzy sphere data into a unitary conformal field theory with a relevant $SO(5)$ singlet scalar, thus strongly supporting the multicriticality scenario of DQCP. The agreement between the conformal bootstrap, QMC and fuzzy sphere results is a surprise towards solving DQCP and decoding the profound phase diagram of the two-dimensional quantum magnets.

AI.tldr: This paper provides strong evidence for the multicriticality scenario of the deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) using conformal bootstrap, showing consistency between bootstrap bounds, Quantum Monte Carlo simulations, and fuzzy sphere data, supporting DQCP as a unitary conformal field theory with a relevant SO(5) singlet scalar.
AI.motivation: The DQCP has been a longstanding controversial topic in condensed matter physics, with two competing scenarios—pseudo-criticality (complex fixed points) and multicriticality (unitary fixed point). This work aims to resolve this debate by providing rigorous evidence for the multicriticality scenario.
AI.method: The authors employ conformal bootstrap with sparse constraints to derive bounds in a three-dimensional parameter space, forming a sharp cone. They use the navigator algorithm to locate the cone's apex and extract extremal solutions, then compare these solutions with QMC and fuzzy sphere data.
AI.result: The bootstrap cone closely matches QMC data, and the extremal bootstrap solutions show striking agreement with fuzzy sphere data, including OPE coefficients and the higher spectrum. This unifies QMC and fuzzy sphere data into a single unitary CFT with a relevant SO(5) singlet scalar.
AI.conclusion: The conformal bootstrap strongly supports the multicriticality scenario of DQCP, suggesting DQCP is a genuine unitary fixed point rather than a pseudo-critical phenomenon, which helps resolve a decades-long controversy and clarifies the phase diagram of two-dimensional quantum magnets.

title: Constraints and Projections for Millicharged Dark Matter in the Sun with Water Cherenkov Neutrino Detectors
summary: Millicharged particles are well-motivated dark matter candidates that have been extensively investigated in terrestrial experiments. Recent studies proposed using the IceCube Neutrino Observatory to search for high-energy neutrinos produced by the capture and annihilation of millicharged dark matter in the Sun, deriving new constraints in the strong interaction regime where the millicharge is $q_χ\sim 10^{-3}$-$10^{-2}$, which extend to small fractional abundances where all existing constraints lose sensitivity. In this work, I point out that the lower energy threshold of water Cherenkov detectors makes Super-Kamiokande and the future Hyper-Kamiokande sensitive to neutrinos from the annihilation of lighter millicharged dark matter, complementing the high-mass reach of IceCube. I find that Super-Kamiokande can constrain previously unexplored parameter space at $m_χ=5$-28 GeV for dark matter fraction of $f_χ=10^{-4.5}$, while Hyper-Kamiokande can improve these constraints and will be sensitive to fractional abundances as small as $f_χ\simeq 5\times 10^{-6}$, nearly an order of magnitude below current IceCube limits.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that water Cherenkov detectors (Super-Kamiokande and future Hyper-Kamiokande) can detect neutrinos from lighter millicharged dark matter annihilation in the Sun, complementing IceCube's high-mass reach and probing previously unexplored parameter space at lower masses (5-28 GeV) with fractional abundances as low as f_χ ~ 5×10⁻⁶.
AI.motivation: Millicharged particles are well-motivated dark matter candidates, but existing constraints lose sensitivity at small fractional abundances. IceCube has recently constrained the strong interaction regime, but only at higher masses. There is a need to probe lower mass ranges of millicharged dark matter.
AI.method: The author analyzes the sensitivity of water Cherenkov detectors (Super-Kamiokande and Hyper-Kamiokande) to high-energy neutrinos produced by capture and annihilation of millicharged dark matter in the Sun, leveraging their lower energy thresholds compared to IceCube.
AI.result: Super-Kamiokande can constrain previously unexplored parameter space at m_χ = 5-28 GeV for f_χ = 10^{-4.5}. Hyper-Kamiokande will be sensitive to fractional abundances as small as f_χ ≃ 5×10^{-6}, nearly an order of magnitude below current IceCube limits.
AI.conclusion: Water Cherenkov detectors complement IceCube's high-mass sensitivity by probing lighter millicharged dark matter, significantly extending the reach to smaller fractional abundances in the low-mass regime.

title: Ramond from Random: Weil-Petersson Volumes for Super-Riemann surfaces with NS Boundaries and R Punctures
summary: The Weil-Petersson (WP) volumes of the (compactified) moduli space of ${N}=1$ supersymmetric Riemann surfaces with Neveu-Schwarz (NS) boundaries are frequently discussed in the literature. Such surfaces can also have marked points called Ramond (R) punctures, where the superconformal structure degenerates. Computing the volumes when these R punctures are included is more challenging for the usual differential and algebraic geometry approaches, and they are therefore less well explored. In particular, the spectral curve describing the inclusion of R punctures is apparently unknown, so far. However, the right random matrix model approach can handle the NS and~R sectors on an equal footing. Such a construction is presented, showing how to use a recently developed technique to readily compute many closed-form formulae for $V^{(2m)}_{g,n}(\{b_i\})$, the WP volumes for genus $g$ with $n$ NS-boundaries of geodesic lengths $b_i$ ($i{=}1,\ldots,n$), and $2m$ R-punctures. Several striking relations between volumes (and subsectors thereof) emerge naturally in this approach. Moreover, the hitherto missing spectral curve is presented, and its use for (re-)deriving the $V^{(2m)}_{g,n}(\{b_i\})$ is demonstrated by using topological recursion.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a random matrix model approach to compute Weil-Petersson volumes of moduli spaces of super-Riemann surfaces with both Neveu-Schwarz boundaries and Ramond punctures, and presents the previously unknown spectral curve for the Ramond sector.
AI.motivation: Computing Weil-Petersson volumes for super-Riemann surfaces with Ramond punctures is challenging using standard differential/algebraic geometry, and the spectral curve for R punctures was unknown. This gap motivates the work.
AI.method: A random matrix model construction that handles Neveu-Schwarz and Ramond sectors on equal footing, combined with topological recursion via the newly derived spectral curve.

title: The Scattering Algebra of Physical Space: Wigner-Covariance and Fields
summary: Following previous work, the Algebra of Physical Space (APS) is used to explore Wigner-covariance and spin/helicity fields within the Constructive Standard Model (CSM) of Particle Physics. The spinor formalism of the APS is used to derive explicit Wigner-covariance of Lorentz spinors, and equivalencies with the CSM are demonstrated via the Scattering Algebra (SA). Constructive fields for spin-1/2 and spin-1 are given in the APS and the necessary maps for Wigner-covariance are proposed. The forms of these spin fields are equivalent to Pauli spinors, thereby serving as a new bridge between the CSM and the study of Quantum Information. It is further seen that spin-1/2 fields of the APS are equivalent to the spin-1/2 fields in the CSM, but the massless cases cannot yet be handled within the SA due to various complications. Similarly, while spin-1 fields exist inside the APS, their SA equivalents deviate from the originally proposed spin-1 fields of the CSM; so further work is needed to prove correspondence between spin-1 fields of the APS and the CSM. Sample Lagrangian densities of the CSM are analyzed using the methods herein, are given geometric interpretations, and are connected to traditional Pauli Theory. Finally, the hff (Higgs and two massive fermions) Lagrangian density is used to determine the first constructive scattering amplitude that is defined purely in terms of the APS. Concerningly, this leads to an anti-Hermitian action term, and this surprise is later confirmed using traditional CSM techniques. Throughout this paper, the illuminating power of Geometric Algebra is clear: Everything has a geometric interpretation, and results can be accomplished matrix-free as well as coordinate-free.

It provides constructive fields for spin-1/2 and spin-1, connects them to Pauli spinors and Quantum Information, and analyzes CSM Lagrangian densities with geometric interpretations. The work reveals an anti-Hermitian action term in the hff scattering amplitude, confirmed by traditional CSM methods, highlighting the geometric clarity of the Geometric Algebra approach.
AI.motivation: To extend the Algebra of Physical Space (APS) framework within the Constructive Standard Model (CSM) to achieve explicit Wigner-covariance for spinor fields, bridge the CSM with Quantum Information via Pauli spinor equivalences, and provide geometric, matrix-free, and coordinate-free interpretations of fundamental particle physics.
AI.method: The spinor formalism of the Algebra of Physical Space (APS) is used to derive Wigner-covariant Lorentz spinors. Equivalencies with the Constructive Standard Model (CSM) are demonstrated via the Scattering Algebra (SA). Constructive fields for spin-1/2 and spin-1 are given in APS, along with maps for Wigner-covariance. Lagrangian densities of the CSM are analyzed geometrically and connected to Pauli Theory.

Spin-1 fields in APS deviate from CSM's originally proposed spin-1 fields, requiring further work. The hff Lagrangian density yields a constructive scattering amplitude with an anti-Hermitian action term, confirmed by traditional CSM techniques.
AI.conclusion: Geometric Algebra (APS) provides illuminating, matrix-free, and coordinate-free geometric interpretations for particle physics. The framework successfully bridges CSM and Quantum Information for spin-1/2 fields, though unresolved issues remain for massless cases and spin-1 field correspondence. The unexpected anti-Hermitian term in the hff amplitude highlights the utility and surprises of this constructive approach.

title: On BPS Branes
summary: We study supersymmetric BPS branes (BPS-B) in supergravity theories. Some of these states are anticipated by BPS black-brane (BPS-BB) solutions of supergravity. In particular, we define and distinguish the cone generated by BPS branes from the subcone of charges that admit BPS black-brane attractor solutions in the infrared limit of the supergravity effective field theory. We denote these cones by $C_{\rm BPS-B}$ and $C_{\rm BPS-BB}$, respectively. We conjecture that, in any supersymmetric theory of quantum gravity, every integrally charged state lying in $C_{\rm BPS-BB}$ is realized by a BPS state in the spectrum. Furthermore, we conjecture and present evidence that when $C_{\rm BPS-B}$ is moduli independent, it can be determined as the cone dual to the $C_{\rm BPS-BB}$ under the electric-magnetic pairing.

AI.tldr: The paper studies supersymmetric BPS branes in supergravity, defining two cones: $C_{\rm BPS-B}$ (all BPS brane charges) and $C_{\rm BPS-BB}$ (charges admitting BPS black-brane attractor solutions). It conjectures that all integrally charged states in $C_{\rm BPS-BB}$ are realized as BPS states, and when $C_{\rm BPS-B}$ is moduli-independent, it is dual to $C_{\rm BPS-BB}$ under electric-magnetic pairing.
AI.motivation: To clarify the relationship between the cone of all BPS brane charges and the cone of charges that admit BPS black-brane attractor solutions in supergravity, and to propose conjectures about which charges are realized as BPS states in quantum gravity.
AI.method: The paper defines two cones—$C_{\rm BPS-B}$ (all BPS brane charges) and $C_{\rm BPS-BB}$ (charges with BPS black-brane attractor solutions)—and analyzes their relationship via electric-magnetic duality. Evidence from supergravity and quantum gravity considerations is presented to support the conjectures.
AI.result: Definition of two distinct cones: $C_{\rm BPS-B}$ and $C_{\rm BPS-BB}$. Two conjectures: (1) every integrally charged state in $C_{\rm BPS-BB}$ is realized as a BPS state; (2) when $C_{\rm BPS-B}$ is moduli-independent, it equals the dual cone of $C_{\rm BPS-BB}$ under the electric-magnetic pairing.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes a framework connecting the cones of BPS brane charges and BPS black-brane attractor solutions, proposing conjectures with supporting evidence that clarify which BPS states must exist in supersymmetric quantum gravity theories.

title: Doubly-strange hidden-charm pentaquarks from the Fermi statistics of the light-quark cloud
summary: We extend the baryo-charmonium picture of pentaquarks -- a color-octet $c\bar c$ core bonded to a color-octet light-quark cloud -- to the doubly-strange sector $c\bar c ssq$. The mass splittings are set entirely by the light cloud, so the only new inputs are the strange-strange couplings $J^{ss}$, fixed by a second application of the chromomagnetic scaling, and an additive strange-mass increment taken from the observed $P_c\!\to\!P_{cs}$ shift. We obtain two negative-parity triplets, one produced with a kaon and one with an antiproton, the lowest kaon-associated $\tfrac12^-$ state near $4.60$~GeV and the antiproton-associated triplet some $120$~MeV below. The robust, distinctive prediction is that the upper two kaon-associated states form a near-degenerate doublet, in sharp contrast to the well-separated triplets of the lighter sectors -- a sparse, fixed-spacing pattern that sets the scheme apart from the molecular and diquark alternatives. The internal splittings follow without adjustment from the measured $P_c$ and $P_{cs}$ spectra; the absolute scale relies on the additive strange-mass ansatz, the main assumption of the extrapolation. The predicted masses agree with recent molecular coupled-channel and QCD sum-rule results.

AI.tldr: The baryo-charmonium pentaquark model is extended to the doubly-strange sector ($c\bar c ssq$), predicting two negative-parity triplets: a kaon-associated $\frac12^-$ state near 4.60 GeV and an antiproton-associated triplet ~120 MeV lower. The upper two kaon-associated states form a near-degenerate doublet, a distinctive pattern that distinguishes this scheme from molecular and diquark alternatives. Predictions agree with recent coupled-channel and QCD sum-rule results.
AI.motivation: To extend the baryo-charmonium picture of pentaquarks to the doubly-strange sector ($c\bar c ssq$) and predict new pentaquark states involving strange quarks.
AI.method: Mass splittings are set by the light cloud using chromomagnetic scaling with strange-strange couplings $J^{ss}$, plus an additive strange-mass increment taken from the observed $P_c \to P_{cs}$ shift. No new parameters beyond the measured $P_c$ and $P_{cs}$ spectra and the strange-mass ansatz.
AI.result: Two negative-parity triplets: a kaon-associated $\frac12^-$ state near 4.60 GeV and an antiproton-associated triplet ~120 MeV lower. The upper two kaon-associated states form a near-degenerate doublet.
AI.conclusion: The scheme yields a sparse, fixed-spacing pattern distinct from molecular and diquark models. Predicted masses agree with recent molecular coupled-channel and QCD sum-rule results.

title: Overlooking 3d dualities from mezzanines and balconies
summary: We derive new 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ dualities with $\mathrm{U}(N)$ gauge groups involving pairs of two-index tensors interacting through a quartic superpotential, (anti)-fundamentals and possibly an adjoint. A strong hint for their validity follows from T-duality on brane setups with O6 planes and stacks of multiple NS fivebranes. These setups engineer two families of 4d models known in the literature as mezzanine and balcony of type $A_k$ and $D_{k+2}$. In 4d these models admit a generalization of Seiberg duality, tested also at the brane level. We study the reduction of such dualities from both the brane and the field theory perspective and we establish the matching of the three-sphere partition functions, assuming the validity of the 4d superconformal indices. The latter is achieved through a double scaling limit, whose structure is dictated by the brane picture, and it requires the validity of new 3d confining dualities for quivers with two gauge nodes. Moreover we provide a proof of these confining dualities via the tensor deconfinement technique.

AI.tldr: The paper derives new 3d 𝒩=2 dualities for U(N) gauge groups with two-index tensors, quartic superpotential, and matter fields, motivated by T-duality on brane setups with O6 planes and NS fivebranes. The dualities are tested via reduction from 4d (mezzanine/balcony type A_k/D_{k+2}) and matching of 3-sphere partition functions using a double scaling limit, supported by new 3d confining dualities proven via tensor deconfinement.
AI.motivation: To establish new 3d 𝒩=2 dualities involving two-index tensor matter fields, guided by T-duality on brane constructions, and to provide rigorous field-theoretic evidence for these dualities.
AI.method: The authors employ T-duality on brane setups with O6 planes and multiple NS fivebranes to engineer 4d models (mezzanine/balcony of type A_k and D_{k+2}), then reduce to 3d. They match 3-sphere partition functions via a double scaling limit derived from the brane picture, and prove confining dualities using the tensor deconfinement technique.
AI.result: New 3d 𝒩=2 dualities are derived and tested. The matching of partition functions is achieved, and new confining dualities for quivers with two gauge nodes are proven.
AI.conclusion: The brane-inspired approach successfully yields valid 3d dualities, and the tensor deconfinement technique provides a rigorous proof of the underlying confining dualities.

title: Light and Strange Baryons in Medium
summary: We solve the Goldstone-boson-exchange (GBE) relativistic constituent quark model of light and strange baryons by using the Faddeev approach. The model reproduces the vacuum mass spectrum of light and strange baryons below $2$ GeV reasonably well. To test the sensitivity of the model to possible medium-induced effects, we vary the masses of the constituent quarks and the exchange bosons, the confinement strength, and the quark-meson coupling constant. In a parametric study, we consider a set of power law scaling relations for these parameters, including some motivated by constituent quark level current algebra relations. We find that the baryon spectrum is most sensitive to the quark-meson coupling constant, and generally observe a decrease in baryon mass with decreasing constituent quark mass. We qualitatively estimate the impact of these mass shifts on ideal-gas baryon yields and yield ratios. Absolute yields can change significantly already for mass shifts of a few $10$~MeV, whereas yield ratios are strongly modified only when the compared baryons have different constituent-quark-mass dependence.

AI.tldr: This paper solves the GBE relativistic constituent quark model for light and strange baryons using the Faddeev approach, reproducing vacuum masses below 2 GeV. It tests medium-induced effects by varying parameters (quark masses, boson masses, confinement strength, quark-meson coupling) under power-law scaling relations, finding the baryon spectrum most sensitive to the quark-meson coupling constant. Mass shifts of a few 10 MeV significantly affect absolute baryon yields, while yield ratios change only when baryons have different constituent-quark-mass dependence.
AI.motivation: To understand how medium-induced effects (e.g., from hot/dense nuclear matter) modify the baryon spectrum within the GBE constituent quark model, and to assess the impact of these modifications on baryon production yields and yield ratios in idealized gas models.
AI.method: The Faddeev approach is used to solve the GBE relativistic constituent quark model. A parametric study is conducted by varying constituent quark masses, exchange boson masses, confinement strength, and quark-meson coupling constant according to power-law scaling relations, including those motivated by constituent quark level current algebra relations.
AI.result: The baryon spectrum is most sensitive to the quark-meson coupling constant. Decreasing constituent quark mass generally lowers baryon masses. Absolute yields change significantly for mass shifts of a few 10 MeV, while yield ratios are strongly modified only when the compared baryons exhibit different constituent-quark-mass dependence.
AI.conclusion: Medium-induced mass shifts can substantially alter absolute baryon yields, but yield ratios are robust unless the baryons have distinct constituent-quark-mass sensitivities. The quark-meson coupling constant is the dominant parameter controlling medium modifications to the baryon spectrum.

title: Normal ordering in string theory and the canonical phase space quantization
comment: arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2509.03237
summary: We consider quantization techniques with a particular emphasis on the phase space quantization, as encountered in quasi-probabilistic descriptions and in string theory. We investigate what is lost by adopting the normal ordering prescription, by revisiting fundamental quantization concepts and the correspondence rules that define the well-known quasi-distributions: the Wigner, Q, and P functions, some of which are inherently ordering dependent. The actual quantum state dictates the necessity of employing discrete countable structures or, alternatively, the complex phase space formulation based on coherent states, and the quasi-distributions depict the existence of the phase space dynamics, of the wave translations and the propagating directions.

AI.tldr: This paper examines phase space quantization, focusing on how normal ordering prescription affects quasi-probabilistic distributions (Wigner, Q, and P functions) and their dependence on quantization correspondence rules, with implications for quantum state representation via discrete structures or coherent state-based complex phase space formulations.
AI.motivation: To investigate what is lost by adopting the normal ordering prescription in quantization, and to revisit fundamental quantization concepts and correspondence rules underlying well-known quasi-distributions.
AI.method: Theoretical analysis of phase space quantization, comparison of quasi-probabilistic descriptions (Wigner, Q, and P functions), and examination of ordering-dependent correspondence rules in the context of coherent states and discrete countable structures.
AI.result: The quantum state determines whether discrete countable structures or complex phase space formulations based on coherent states are necessary; quasi-distributions reveal phase space dynamics, wave translations, and propagating directions.
AI.conclusion: Normal ordering prescription incurs specific losses in quantization; the choice between discrete and continuous phase space representations is dictated by the quantum state itself.

title: Hidden Harmonic Structure of Fermion Masses and Flavor
summary: We investigate a harmonic interpretation of the hidden flavor coordinates (Q,G,C) introduced previously in a low-rank ternary description of the fermion mass spectrum. In this picture, the generation coordinate is associated with the odd harmonic sequence (1,3,5), allowing the fermion mass formula to be expressed in a compact harmonic form. The logarithmic mass spectrum then acquires an additive structure in which the hidden coordinates contribute directly to the observed hierarchy of fermion masses. We further argue that the scalar quantity (L=QG+C), which successfully organizes the fermion spectrum, does not uniquely identify a fermion state. This observation motivates the introduction of the full hidden-coordinate vector X=(Q,G,C) and a geometric interpretation of flavor in terms of distances, relative orientations, and antisymmetric invariants defined within the hidden-coordinate space. The harmonic framework also suggests a possible extension beyond the fermion sector. Combining the fermionic harmonic modes naturally generates the even sequence (2,4,6,8,10), which exhibits a suggestive correspondence with the electroweak and Higgs scales. While this correspondence remains speculative, it points toward a common harmonic structure underlying both fermionic and bosonic states. Although the framework is exploratory, it indicates that fermion masses, flavor organization, and bosonic excitations may represent different manifestations of a deeper hidden harmonic structure.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a harmonic interpretation of hidden flavor coordinates (Q,G,C) to explain the fermion mass hierarchy, where the generation coordinate follows an odd harmonic sequence (1,3,5), and suggests that combining fermionic modes yields even sequences (2,4,6,8,10) that may correspond to electroweak/Higgs scales, implying a common harmonic structure underlying both fermions and bosons.
AI.motivation: To provide a harmonic interpretation of previously introduced hidden flavor coordinates (Q,G,C) that can explain the observed hierarchy of fermion masses and potentially unify the description of fermionic and bosonic sectors through a common harmonic structure.
AI.method: The study reinterprets the flavor coordinates (Q,G,C) using harmonic sequences: the generation coordinate G is associated with odd harmonics (1,3,5). It introduces the full hidden-coordinate vector X=(Q,G,C) and applies geometric concepts such as distances, relative orientations, and antisymmetric invariants. It then extends the harmonic framework by combining fermionic modes to generate even sequences (2,4,6,8,10).
AI.result: The hidden coordinates contribute additively to the logarithmic mass spectrum, organizing the fermion hierarchy. The scalar L=QG+C does not uniquely identify fermion states, motivating a geometric flavor interpretation. The even harmonic sequence derived from fermionic modes shows speculative correspondence with electroweak and Higgs scales.
AI.conclusion: Fermion masses, flavor organization, and bosonic excitations may be different manifestations of a deeper hidden harmonic structure, though the framework remains exploratory.

title: Hawking--Page Universality, Thermodynamic Dipoles and Categorical Defects
summary: We reconsider the Hawking--Page transition using the common thermodynamic vector field whose zeros include the Davies and Hawking--Page points. In the elementary AdS branch their winding numbers are $w_{\rm D}=-1$ and $w_{\rm HP}=+1$, so the pair has zero total charge but a non-zero signed first moment. After normalization by the Davies scales this moment gives the familiar universal ratios $C_S$ and $C_T$; in four dimensions $C_S=2$ and $C_T=2/\sqrt{3}-1$. We check the construction for Schwarzschild--AdS, grand-canonical Reissner--Nordström--AdS, charged non-rotating black holes in arbitrary dimension, and Kerr--AdS at fixed angular velocity. The same reduced geometry gives a barrier $B=1/3$ in four dimensions and $B(d)=1/[(d-1)(d-3)]$. Finally we propose a formulation involving a defect-resolved version for categorical or non-invertible symmetry sectors.

AI.tldr: The paper re-examines the Hawking-Page transition using a thermodynamic vector field formalism, where Davies and Hawking-Page points appear as zeros with winding numbers -1 and +1. After normalization, these yield universal ratios C_S and C_T (C_S=2, C_T=2/√3-1 in 4D). The construction is validated across multiple black hole systems and extended to a defect-resolved formulation for non-invertible symmetry sectors.
AI.motivation: To provide a novel topological perspective on the Hawking-Page transition by interpreting the Davies and Hawking-Page points as zeros of a thermodynamic vector field, thereby revealing universal structure and conserved quantities.
AI.method: Introduces a common thermodynamic vector field whose zeros include Davies and Hawking-Page points; computes winding numbers and signed first moments; normalizes by Davies scales to obtain universal ratios; tests on Schwarzschild-AdS, Reissner-Nordström-AdS, charged black holes in arbitrary dimensions, and Kerr-AdS at fixed angular velocity.
AI.result: Davies point has winding number -1, Hawking-Page point +1 (total charge zero, non-zero signed first moment). Normalized first moment yields universal ratios C_S=2 and C_T=2/√3-1 in 4D. The reduced geometry gives barrier B=1/3 in 4D and B(d)=1/[(d-1)(d-3)] in general dimensions.
AI.conclusion: The thermodynamic vector field approach unifies the Davies and Hawking-Page points under a topological framework with universal ratios, and can be extended to defect-resolved formulations for categorical or non-invertible symmetry sectors.

title: The Non-perturbative term for the Axial-vector Form Factor of Pion Decay
summary: The axial-vector form factor for the decay of pion $π^{+} \rightarrow γ+ e^{+} + ν_e$ is calculated by using the pseudovector coupling pion-nucleon interaction with the non-perturbative term. The self-energy is approximated by the lowest-order constant. The parameter is significant to improve the value of the form factor as well as the vector form factor in our previous study.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates the axial-vector form factor for the pion decay π⁺ → γ + e⁺ + νₑ using pseudovector coupling pion-nucleon interaction with a non-perturbative term, approximating self-energy by the lowest-order constant to improve the form factor value.
AI.motivation: To improve the calculation of the axial-vector form factor for the radiative pion decay π⁺ → γ + e⁺ + νₑ, building upon previous work on the vector form factor.
AI.method: Uses pseudovector coupling pion-nucleon interaction with a non-perturbative term, approximating the self-energy by the lowest-order constant.
AI.result: The introduced parameter significantly improves the value of both the axial-vector form factor and the vector form factor compared to the previous study.
AI.conclusion: The non-perturbative term and lowest-order self-energy approximation yield an improved axial-vector form factor for the radiative pion decay process.

title: Chiral Plasma under Strong Magnetic Fields: A Holographic Analysis of Transport Phenomena
summary: Chiral plasma appears in several areas of physics, historically starting from primordial plasma in the early Universe, then in quark-gluon plasma produced in heavy ion collisions, and, more recently, in Dirac and Weyl semimetals. The major signature of the plasma is the non-conservation of the axial current due to the chiral anomaly and the emergence of new, anomaly-induced transport phenomena. In this paper, we study the plasma exposed to arbitrarily strong constant magnetic and weak electric fields. Employing all-order gradient resummation, we write down constitutive relations for electric and axial currents parameterized by thirteen momentum- and magnetic- field-dependent transport coefficient functions. The latter are computed utilizing a theoretical lab for a realistic plasma, namely a holographic $U(1)_V \times U(1)_A$ Maxwell--Chern--Simons theory in Schwarzschild--AdS$_5$, in the probe limit. As an application, we revisit the phenomena of negative magnetoresistance and chiral magnetic waves, beyond the naive hydrodynamic limit.

AI.tldr: The paper studies chiral plasma in strong magnetic and weak electric fields using holographic methods, deriving transport coefficient functions and revisiting negative magnetoresistance and chiral magnetic waves beyond hydrodynamic limits.
AI.motivation: To understand anomaly-induced transport phenomena in chiral plasma under arbitrarily strong magnetic fields, going beyond the hydrodynamic limit.
AI.method: All-order gradient resummation combined with a holographic U(1)_V × U(1)_A Maxwell-Chern-Simons theory in Schwarzschild-AdS_5 in the probe limit.
AI.result: Constitutive relations for electric and axial currents parameterized by thirteen momentum- and magnetic-field-dependent transport coefficient functions, computed holographically.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables revisiting negative magnetoresistance and chiral magnetic waves beyond the naive hydrodynamic limit.

title: Tensor Decomposition for Energy-Momentum Correlation Functions
summary: We establish the general functional form of the energy-momentum-tensor two-point function in Euclidean coordinate space at zero and finite temperature. The full correlation function is first decomposed into its fundamental tensorial structures based on the remaining rotational symmetry. We use energy-momentum conservation to derive differential relations between the resulting component functions. Using these constraints, the full set of component functions of the correlator can finally be represented in the form of a smaller set of spectral functions. Finally, we show how to use these techniques for more efficient future lattice investigations.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes the general functional form of the energy-momentum-tensor two-point function in Euclidean coordinate space at zero and finite temperature, decomposes it into tensorial structures, derives differential relations using energy-momentum conservation, and reduces the component functions to a smaller set of spectral functions for more efficient lattice investigations.
AI.motivation: To provide a general, systematic functional decomposition of the energy-momentum-tensor two-point function in Euclidean space (zero and finite temperature) and reduce its component functions to a minimal set of spectral functions, enabling more efficient future lattice QCD computations.
AI.method: The correlator is first decomposed into fundamental tensorial structures based on the remaining rotational symmetry. Energy-momentum conservation is then used to derive differential relations between the resulting component functions. These constraints allow the full set of component functions to be represented in terms of a smaller set of spectral functions.

AI.conclusion: The derived formalism provides a systematic framework that can be applied for more efficient future lattice investigations of the energy-momentum-tensor correlator.

title: Pair creation amplitudes for a real scalar field coupled to a time-dependent surface in d+1 dimensions
summary: We study the pair creation phenomenon for a real scalar field $\varphi$ in the presence of a surface that undergoes time-dependent deformations, while imposing Dirichlet-like boundary conditions. Including terms up to fourth order in the departure of the surface from an infinite plane, we present results for the angular dependence of the emission rate for the vacuum-to-pair process as a function of the geometry and the dynamics of the surface, as well as of the momenta of the emitted pair. We check the consistency of the leading contribution with previous results obtained from the imaginary part of the effective action, and clarify how the relation between exclusive probabilities and the imaginary part of the effective action is modified at fourth order by the opening of a two-pair channel.

AI.tldr: The paper studies pair creation of a real scalar field near a dynamically deforming surface with Dirichlet boundary conditions, computing emission rates up to fourth order in surface deformations and showing how the two-pair channel modifies the relation between exclusive probabilities and the imaginary part of the effective action.
AI.motivation: To understand how time-dependent geometric deformations of a surface (beyond an infinite plane) influence vacuum-to-pair creation processes, and to clarify the connection between exclusive probabilities and the effective action at higher orders.
AI.method: The analysis includes terms up to fourth order in the deviation from an infinite plane, imposes Dirichlet boundary conditions on a real scalar field, and computes the angular dependence of the emission rate for the vacuum-to-pair process.
AI.result: Results for the angular dependence of the emission rate as a function of surface geometry/dynamics and pair momenta; consistency with leading-order results from the imaginary part of the effective action; identification of a modification at fourth order due to the opening of a two-pair channel.
AI.conclusion: The leading contribution agrees with previous effective-action results, but at fourth order, the two-pair channel alters the relationship between exclusive probabilities and the imaginary part of the effective action.

title: Constraints on the Higgs-gluon effective coupling through $h \to γγ$ decays at the LHC

AI.tldr: This paper studies the pp→h→γγ process in the HPOprodMFV_UFO model, simulating 26 parameter points with |κ_g| from 0.6 to 1.4 using MadGraph5, Pythia8, Delphes, and MadAnalysis5. It confirms quadratic scaling σ ∝ κ_g², reports SM cross section σ_SM = 0.04067 ± 0.00008 pb, and derives constraints |κ_g| ∈ [0.80, 1.20] at 68% CL and [0.70, 1.30] at 95% CL, consistent with ATLAS/CMS results.
