title: On Calabi-Yau Threefolds For Unified LVS Inflation
summary: Fibre inflation, Poly-instanton inflation and (Loop) Blow-up inflation are among the most popular Kähler moduli based inflationary models realized in the standard LARGE volume scenarios (LVS). In this article, we present a unified framework in which all these three LVS inflationary models can be realized by using (different orientifolds of) a single Calabi-Yau (CY) threefold. In fact, the desired CY threefold needs to have a K3- or ${\mathbb T}^4$-fibration structure along with two diagonal del Pezzo divisors, and a so-called `Wilson' divisor which corresponds to a surface realized as a ${\mathbb P}^1$ fibration over ${\mathbb T}^2$s. For classification purpose, we perform a detailed scan of the CY geometries with $1 \leq h^{1,1}({\rm CY}) \leq 6$ that arise from the triangulation of the four-dimensional reflexive polytopes of the Kreuzer-Skarke database. In this regard, after scanning around 100,000 CY geometries and the corresponding topologies of around a million of toric divisors, we find two CY threefolds satisfying these requirements for $1 \leq h^{1,1}({\rm CY}) \leq 4$, while there are 14 and 45 candidate CY geometries for $h^{1,1}({\rm CY}) = 5$ and $h^{1,1}({\rm CY}) = 6$, respectively. We discuss the extended applications of such CY threefolds for cosmological model building in string theoretic frameworks.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a unified framework for three Kähler moduli inflation models (Fibre, Poly-instanton, Loop Blow-up) using a single Calabi-Yau threefold with specific divisor structures, identifying 14 (h¹·¹=5) and 45 (h¹·¹=6) candidate CY geometries from scanning ~100,000 geometries in the Kreuzer-Skarke database.
AI.motivation: To unify three popular LVS inflationary models (Fibre inflation, Poly-instanton inflation, Loop Blow-up inflation) under a single CY threefold framework, enabling systematic cosmological model building in string theory.
AI.method: Systematic scan of CY threefolds with 1 ≤ h¹·¹ ≤ 6 from triangulated 4D reflexive polytopes of the Kreuzer-Skarke database, analyzing ~100,000 CY geometries and ~1 million toric divisors to identify those with K3/T⁴-fibration, two diagonal del Pezzo divisors, and a Wilson divisor (P¹ fibration over T²).
AI.result: Found 2 candidate CY threefolds for 1 ≤ h¹·¹ ≤ 4, 14 candidates for h¹·¹ = 5, and 45 candidates for h¹·¹ = 6 that satisfy all required divisor structures for the unified inflationary framework.
AI.conclusion: The identified CY threefolds provide a unified geometric realization for the three LVS inflationary models, with potential for extended cosmological model building in string theory.

title: $Λ(1670)$ production in the $ψ(3686) \to Λ\bar Λη$ reaction
summary: We perform a calculation of the invariant mass distributions in the $ψ(3686) \to Λ\bar Λη$ reaction, where a neat peak for the excitation of the $Λ(1670)$ and $\bar Λ(1670)$ in the $ηΛ$ and $η\bar Λ$ mass distributions, respectively, is observed. Our approach uses the fact that the $ψ(3686)$, a $c \bar c$ state, is a singlet of SU(3) in the $u,d,s$ quarks and constructs the two flavor structures allowed with a pseudoscalar meson, a baryon and an antibaryon. The resonance peaks come from the final state interaction of meson baryon pairs, which generate the $ Λ(1670)$ in our approach. With a reasonable relative weight of the two flavor structures, the only free parameter of the theory, we are able to get the three mass distributions in good agreement with experiment, giving extra support to the molecular structure of the $Λ(1670)$ resonance. The agreement with data improves with an extra resonance contribution with mass around 2200 MeV.

AI.tldr: The paper calculates invariant mass distributions in ψ(3686) → ΛΛ̄η, identifying Λ(1670) and Λ̄(1670) peaks in ηΛ and ηΛ̄ spectra, supporting the molecular structure of Λ(1670) via final state interactions, with improved agreement using an extra ~2200 MeV resonance.
AI.motivation: To calculate invariant mass distributions in ψ(3686) → ΛΛ̄η and investigate the nature of the Λ(1670) resonance, particularly testing its molecular structure through final state interactions of meson-baryon pairs.
AI.method: Uses the SU(3) singlet nature of ψ(3686) (c̄c state) to construct two flavor structures with a pseudoscalar meson, baryon, and antibaryon. The Λ(1670) is generated via final state interaction of meson-baryon pairs. The relative weight of the two flavor structures is the only free parameter.
AI.result: The model reproduces three mass distributions in good agreement with experiment, supporting the molecular structure of Λ(1670). Agreement improves with an additional resonance around 2200 MeV.
AI.conclusion: The results provide extra support for the molecular (meson-baryon) structure of the Λ(1670) resonance.

title: Spacetime from Operator Algebras
summary: Under suitable assumptions, geometric objects such as the spacetime metric and curvature tensor can be reconstructed from the algebra of operators of quantized matter fields in the limit of vanishing Newton's constant. In this framework, the full non-linear Einstein equations can be expressed in the language of operator algebras, extending Jacobson's derivation without invoking the area law for Bekenstein-Hawking entropy. These assumptions can then be used as a criterion for determining whether the semiclassical limit of a given quantum theory admits an emergent gravitational description. Going in the other direction, the discrete spectrum of a holographic theory at finite N can be modelled by adding non-perturbative corrections to semiclassical operator algebras. The type III von Neumann algebra that arises in the vanishing Newton's constant limit can be enlarged by adjoining its modular Hamiltonian. A random matrix theory completion of this enlarged algebra, followed by ensemble averaging, results in a type I von Neumann algebra whose minimal projectors approximate those of the underlying microstates. In the case of an eternal black hole, the dimension of the type I algebra equals the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy with universal logarithmic corrections. The complexity of probe operators in the boundary theory provides a diagnostic of the validity of the corresponding bulk semiclassical effective field theory.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that spacetime geometry and Einstein equations can be reconstructed from operator algebras of quantized matter fields in the G→0 limit, and that holographic theories at finite N yield type I von Neumann algebras via random matrix completions, with black hole entropy emerging naturally.
AI.motivation: To derive the full non-linear Einstein equations from operator algebra language (extending Jacobson's derivation without relying on the Bekenstein-Hawking area law), and to understand how semiclassical limits of quantum theories can admit emergent gravitational descriptions.
AI.method: The approach uses type III von Neumann algebras in the G→0 limit, enlarged by modular Hamiltonians. A random matrix theory completion of the enlarged algebra followed by ensemble averaging yields a type I von Neumann algebra whose minimal projectors approximate microstates. Operator complexity in the boundary theory diagnoses bulk semiclassical EFT validity.
AI.result: The type I algebra's dimension for an eternal black hole equals the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy with universal logarithmic corrections. Non-perturbative corrections to semiclassical operator algebras model the discrete spectrum of holographic theories at finite N.
AI.conclusion: Geometric reconstruction from operator algebras is possible under suitable assumptions, providing a criterion for emergent gravity in quantum theories. The framework connects random matrix theory, von Neumann algebras, and black hole thermodynamics.

title: Hunting for QCD Instantons
summary: Instantons are non-perturbative classical solutions which describe transitions between different QCD vacua. They have never been observed experimentally. We consider the signatures of the instanton (sphaleron) production events and the main QCD backgrounds. The possibilities to search for the QCD instantons in the diffractive (i.e. with a large rapidity gap) events at the LHC and via the spin-spin correlations between two hyperons at NICA are discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper discusses the experimental search for QCD instantons (sphalerons), non-perturbative classical solutions describing transitions between QCD vacua, focusing on diffractive events at the LHC and hyperon spin-spin correlations at NICA.
AI.motivation: Instantons have never been experimentally observed despite being a key theoretical prediction of QCD; the paper aims to identify feasible experimental signatures and search strategies for these elusive non-perturbative objects.
AI.method: The authors analyze signatures of instanton/sphaleron production events, evaluate main QCD backgrounds, and propose two search channels: diffractive events with large rapidity gaps at the LHC, and spin-spin correlations between two hyperons at NICA.
AI.result: Identification of distinct instanton signatures and characterization of dominant QCD background processes; assessment of feasibility for LHC diffractive searches and NICA hyperon spin correlation measurements.
AI.conclusion: Searching for QCD instantons is possible through diffractive events at the LHC and hyperon spin correlations at NICA, offering promising experimental avenues to observe these non-perturbative QCD phenomena.

title: Supersymmetry of the static Reissner-Nordström black hole in Bertotti-Robinson ($\mathrm{AdS}_2 \times \mathbb{S}^2$)
summary: We examine supersymmetry of charged and accelerating black holes embedded in a Bertotti-Robinson universe, in the context of $N=2$, $D=4$ supergravity. After a review of the solution, we study the constraints that guarantee supersymmetry and explicitly compute the Killing spinors of the spacetime. We show that the supersymmetric solution saturates the BPS bound, and we use this result to compute the mass of the black hole and to analyze the thermodynamics of the solution. Finally, we present a generalization of the extremal solution to include the cosmological constant.

AI.tldr: This paper examines supersymmetric charged and accelerating black holes in Bertotti-Robinson spacetime within N=2, D=4 supergravity, computes Killing spinors, shows BPS bound saturation, derives black hole mass and thermodynamics, and generalizes to include a cosmological constant.
AI.motivation: To understand the supersymmetry properties of charged, accelerating black holes in a Bertotti-Robinson (anti-de Sitter) background and to establish their BPS nature, enabling mass and thermodynamic analysis.
AI.method: Reviewing the charged accelerating black hole solution in Bertotti-Robinson spacetime; imposing supersymmetry constraints; explicitly computing Killing spinors; using BPS saturation to derive the mass; analyzing thermodynamics; extending to include a cosmological constant.
AI.result: The supersymmetric solution saturates the BPS bound, allowing the black hole mass to be computed; thermodynamics of the solution are analyzed; the extremal solution is generalized to incorporate the cosmological constant.
AI.conclusion: Charged accelerating black holes in Bertotti-Robinson spacetime can be supersymmetric (BPS), with their mass and thermodynamics derived from the BPS condition, and the framework extends to include cosmological constant effects.

title: Scattering Theory
comment: 13 pages, 6 figures, Invited contribution to the Encyclopedia of Particle Physics
summary: This chapter provides an overview of the fundamental framework of scattering theory, which is widely used in particle physics to describe and interpret interactions among elementary particles. We explore how transition amplitudes enable the analysis of data from scattering experiments and the extraction of resonance parameters. The concepts and methods discussed are essential for understanding processes studied at major accelerator facilities worldwide and in a broad range of hadronic and nuclear systems.

AI.tldr: Overview of scattering theory's fundamental framework in particle physics, covering transition amplitudes, resonance parameter extraction, and applications to accelerator experiments and hadronic/nuclear systems.
AI.motivation: To provide a comprehensive introduction to scattering theory as the essential mathematical and conceptual tool for describing elementary particle interactions and interpreting experimental data from accelerator facilities.
AI.method: Presentation of the fundamental scattering theory framework, focusing on transition amplitudes as the key mathematical objects connecting theoretical predictions to experimental observations.
AI.result: A foundational understanding of how scattering theory enables the analysis of experimental data and extraction of resonance parameters from particle interactions.
AI.conclusion: Scattering theory concepts and methods are essential for understanding particle physics processes studied at major accelerator facilities and across hadronic and nuclear systems.

title: Efficient AI-Inspired Reduction of Feynman Integrals via Tube Seeding
summary: In this paper, we use machine learning to discover a new seeding strategy for integration-by-parts reduction of Feynman integrals, which is a frequent bottleneck in state-of-the-art calculations in theoretical particle and gravitational-wave physics. Our strategy allows us to reduce multi-loop integrals with large numerator powers via essentially the standard Laporta algorithm but with a sparse selection of seed integrals that grows only linearly with the numerator power, whereas existing strategies lead to growth with a polynomial power that increases with the complexity of the integral being reduced. The seeds are restricted to a thin tube-like region that connects the target integral to the master integrals along a zigzag path. We demonstrate the power of our approach by reducing non-planar 2-loop 5-point integrals of rank 20 with numerical kinematics over a finite field, which is prohibitively difficult for the Laporta algorithm with conventional seeding. Going beyond individual integrals, we further demonstrate the reduction of a complete set of top-level rank-10 integrals by dividing the target integrals into several chunks, each of which can be solved by our sparse seeding strategy with considerably less time and a significantly lower memory footprint than other state-of-the-art strategies, making the approach well-suited for phenomenological applications. We provide a proof-of-principle implementation on GitHub at https://github.com/andreslunagodoy/tube_seeding.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a machine learning-based sparse seeding strategy for integration-by-parts reduction of Feynman integrals, which reduces seed growth from polynomial to linear with numerator power, demonstrated on challenging non-planar 2-loop 5-point integrals up to rank 20.
AI.motivation: Integration-by-parts reduction of Feynman integrals is a bottleneck in high-precision theoretical calculations for particle physics and gravitational-wave physics; existing seeding strategies lead to polynomial growth in seed count with numerator power, making high-rank integrals computationally prohibitive.
AI.method: A machine learning-discovered seeding strategy that restricts seeds to a thin tube-like region connecting target integrals to master integrals along a zigzag path, reducing seed count growth from polynomial to linear with numerator power; demonstrated on non-planar 2-loop 5-point integrals over finite fields.
AI.result: Successfully reduced non-planar 2-loop 5-point integrals of rank 20 with numerical kinematics, which is prohibitively difficult for standard Laporta with conventional seeding; also demonstrated reduction of complete set of top-level rank-10 integrals with lower time and memory footprint than other state-of-the-art strategies.
AI.conclusion: The tube-like sparse seeding strategy makes high-rank multi-loop integral reduction feasible for phenomenological applications; a proof-of-principle implementation is publicly available on GitHub.

title: Isospin-symmetry in $pp$ and $AA$ collisions
summary: The hypothesis of a violation of isospin-symmetry in pp and AA collisions is discussed. We show that the ratio of charged-to-neutral kaon cross sections, $R_K~=~\frac{σ_{K^+}+σ_{K^-}}{2σ_{K^0_S}}$, calculated within the similarity approach, including the gluon transverse momentum dependence (TMD) at low QCD scales, and using the Lund model in the form of the MC generator PYTHIA, is above 1 at energies $\sqrt{s}$ up to 20 GeV, even in the case of isospin-symmetry conservation. It decreases to 1, when the energy rises to a few TeV (ALICE data). The reason for this is related to the dynamics of kaon production. This energy behavior of $R_K$ does practically not depend on the sort of beam or target.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the charged-to-neutral kaon ratio RK in pp and AA collisions, showing it exceeds 1 at low energies (up to 20 GeV) even with isospin symmetry conservation, and decreases to 1 at TeV scales (ALICE data), explained by kaon production dynamics with minimal dependence on beam/target type.
AI.motivation: To examine whether the charged-to-neutral kaon ratio RK deviates from 1 due to isospin symmetry violation in pp and AA collisions, and to understand the energy dependence of this observable.
AI.method: The RK ratio is calculated using three approaches: the similarity approach, including gluon transverse momentum dependence (TMD) at low QCD scales, and the Lund model implemented in the PYTHIA MC generator.
AI.result: RK > 1 at energies up to 20 GeV even when isospin symmetry is conserved; RK decreases to 1 as energy rises to a few TeV (consistent with ALICE data). This behavior is largely independent of beam or target type.
AI.conclusion: The observed energy-dependent RK behavior stems from kaon production dynamics rather than isospin symmetry violation, and the ratio approaches unity at high energies.

title: Does the Weinberg angle allow a local hidden-variable description for the leptonic decays of an entangled $ZZ$ pair?
summary: Quantum entanglement in diboson systems offers a useful testing ground for exploring the boundary between quantum-mechanical correlations and classical descriptions based on local hidden variables. In this work, we study the spin-polarization state of a $Z_1Z_2$ pair produced from the decay of a spin-0 particle and investigate whether the angular correlations predicted by quantum field theory (QFT) in the leptonic decays $Z_1(\to e^-_1 e^+_1)Z_2(\to e^-_2 e^+_2)$ can be reproduced by a local hidden-variable theory (LHVT) under angular-momentum conservation. By matching the LHVT angular distribution to the QFT prediction coefficient by coefficient, we derive the conditions under which an LHVT construction exists. For the case $w\neq 0$, we show that, apart from trivial product-state configurations, an LHVT construction exists only for a unique entangled pure state, corresponding to $a_1=a_3=-a_2=1/\sqrt{3}$ and $b_2=b_3=0$, together with a restricted window of the weak-mixing angle $θ_W$. For $w=0$, we derive a necessary and sufficient criterion for the existence of an LHVT construction in terms of a closed set of algebraic and positivity conditions. As an application, we consider the phenomenologically relevant interaction $sZ^μZ_μ$ and show that an LHVT construction exists at threshold $m_s=2m_Z$, whereas it does not exist for $m_s>2m_Z$.

AI.tldr: This paper studies quantum entanglement in Z₁Z₂ diboson systems from spin-0 particle decay, investigating whether QFT angular correlations can be reproduced by local hidden-variable theories (LHVT) under angular-momentum conservation. It finds LHVT constructions exist only for a specific entangled pure state with a restricted weak-mixing angle window, and for the sZ^μZ_μ interaction, an LHVT construction exists at threshold m_s=2m_Z but not for m_s>2m_Z.
AI.motivation: To explore the boundary between quantum-mechanical correlations and classical local hidden-variable descriptions in diboson systems, and to test whether QFT predictions for Z-boson pair angular correlations can be reproduced by an LHVT under angular-momentum conservation.
AI.method: The authors match the LHVT angular distribution to the QFT prediction coefficient by coefficient, derive algebraic and positivity conditions for LHVT existence, and analyze specific cases (w≠0, w=0) as well as the phenomenological sZ^μZ_μ interaction.
AI.result: For w≠0, an LHVT construction exists only for a unique entangled pure state (a₁=a₃=-a₂=1/√3, b₂=b₃=0) within a restricted θ_W window. For w=0, a necessary and sufficient criterion is derived. For sZ^μZ_μ, LHVT exists at threshold m_s=2m_Z but not for m_s>2m_Z.
AI.conclusion: Quantum entanglement in Z-boson pairs from spin-0 decay cannot generally be described by local hidden-variable theories except under very specific conditions, highlighting the quantum nature of the correlations in these diboson systems.

title: The Gravitational Form Factor of the Pion in Perturbative QCD with a Dilaton Interaction
summary: We investigate the pion gravitational form factors (GFFs) at intermediate and large momentum transfer within the framework of QCD factorization. Our analysis centers on the non-Abelian $TJJ$ correlator, which couples the local QCD energy-momentum tensor to two external gluon fields and explicitly encodes the perturbative effects of the trace anomaly. We demonstrate how this quantum anomaly induces a scalar, dilaton-like contribution to the hard-scattering kernel. To ensure field-theoretic consistency, a careful separation of the quark and gluon sectors is performed, accounting for the modifications introduced by gauge-fixing terms and Slavnov-Taylor identities on the off-shell gluonic structure. To obtain realistic phenomenological predictions and regulate soft-gluon endpoint divergences in the hard kernel, we implement the Sudakov resummation framework coupled with a Gaussian model for the pion's transverse-momentum-dependent wave function. We show that the resulting anomaly-induced corrections significantly modify the behavior of the pion GFFs at large momentum transfer, leaving a unique imprint on the trace sector and the $D$-term.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates pion gravitational form factors (GFFs) using QCD factorization, focusing on the non-Abelian TJJ correlator coupling the energy-momentum tensor to two gluon fields. The trace anomaly induces a scalar dilaton-like contribution. Using Sudakov resummation and a Gaussian transverse-momentum-dependent wave function, the authors show anomaly-induced corrections significantly modify GFF behavior at large momentum transfer, particularly in the trace sector and D-term.
AI.motivation: To understand how the QCD trace anomaly affects pion gravitational form factors at intermediate and large momentum transfer, and to provide field-theoretically consistent phenomenological predictions for these quantities.
AI.method: QCD factorization framework analyzing the non-Abelian TJJ correlator; separation of quark and gluon sectors with gauge-fixing and Slavnov-Taylor identities; Sudakov resummation with Gaussian transverse-momentum-dependent wave function to regulate soft-gluon endpoint divergences.
AI.result: Anomaly-induced corrections significantly modify pion GFFs at large momentum transfer, leaving distinct imprints on the trace sector and D-term.
AI.conclusion: The trace anomaly contributes a scalar dilaton-like term to the hard-scattering kernel that produces measurable modifications to pion GFFs, emphasizing the need for consistent field-theoretic treatment of gluonic contributions.

title: Magnetic Moment of Octet Baryons in Isospin Asymmetric Magnetized Strange Matter
summary: We investigate the magnetic moments of octet baryons in isospin asymmetric strange hadronic matter under strong external magnetic fields within a unified theoretical framework by combining the chiral SU(3) quark mean field (CQMF) model with the chiral constituent quark ($χ$CQM) model. At finite temperature, the inclusion of Dirac sea (DS) effect leads to magnetic catalysis attributing to the enhancement of scalar condensates with increasing magnetic field strength. As a consequence, the effective masses of the octet baryons exhibit a monotonic increase as a function of magnetic field. The results highlight the crucial role of vacuum polarization effects in determining the electromagnetic properties of baryons in strongly magnetized matter having relevance in heavy-ion collision and compact stars.

AI.tldr: This paper studies magnetic moments of octet baryons in isospin asymmetric strange hadronic matter under strong magnetic fields by combining CQMF and χCQM models. The Dirac sea effect induces magnetic catalysis, increasing scalar condensates and baryon effective masses with magnetic field strength. Vacuum polarization effects are crucial for electromagnetic properties in magnetized matter relevant to heavy-ion collisions and compact stars.
AI.motivation: To understand the electromagnetic properties of octet baryons in strongly magnetized, isospin asymmetric strange hadronic matter, which is relevant for heavy-ion collision experiments and compact star astrophysics.
AI.method: Combines the chiral SU(3) quark mean field (CQMF) model with the chiral constituent quark (χCQM) model at finite temperature, including Dirac sea (DS) effects.
AI.result: The Dirac sea effect leads to magnetic catalysis via enhanced scalar condensates with increasing magnetic field, causing monotonic increase in effective baryon masses.
AI.conclusion: Vacuum polarization effects are crucial for determining baryon electromagnetic properties in strongly magnetized matter with implications for heavy-ion collisions and compact stars.

title: Hidden Flavor Geometry and Yukawa Structure from Hidden Coordinates
summary: We investigate a harmonic interpretation of the hidden flavor coordinates (Q,G,C) previously introduced in a low-rank ternary description of the fermion mass spectrum. The generation coordinate is associated with the odd harmonic mode sequence n_G = (1,3,5), allowing the fermion mass ansatz to be rewritten in a compact harmonic form. The corresponding logarithmic spectrum reveals an additive structure in which the hidden coordinates contribute directly to the observed mass hierarchy. We argue that the projected quantity L = QG + C, which organizes the fermion masses, does not uniquely characterize a fermion state. This motivates the introduction of the full hidden-coordinate vector X = (Q,G,C) and a geometric interpretation of flavor based on coordinate separations and antisymmetric invariants defined within the hidden-coordinate space. The harmonic framework further suggests a possible extension beyond the fermion sector. Combining the fermionic harmonic modes generates the bosonic sequence n_B = (2,4,6,8,10), which exhibits a suggestive correspondence with the electroweak and Higgs scales. Although the resulting framework remains exploratory, it suggests that fermion masses, flavor structure, and bosonic states may reflect different aspects of a common hidden harmonic organization.

Fermion generations map to odd harmonic modes n_G=(1,3,5); bosonic states emerge from combining fermionic modes, yielding n_B=(2,4,6,8,10) that align with electroweak/Higgs scales. The authors propose a geometric flavor space based on the full coordinate vector X=(Q,G,C).

AI.method: The generation coordinate G is associated with odd harmonic modes (1,3,5). The mass ansatz is rewritten in harmonic form, revealing additive structure. The full hidden-coordinate vector X=(Q,G,C) is introduced, with geometric flavor interpretation via coordinate separations and antisymmetric invariants. Combining fermionic harmonic modes generates bosonic sequences n_B=(2,4,6,8,10).
AI.result: The projected quantity L=QG+C insufficiently characterizes fermion states, motivating the vector X. The harmonic framework generates bosonic sequences that correspond suggestively to electroweak and Higgs scales.
AI.conclusion: Fermion masses, flavor structure, and bosonic states may reflect different aspects of a common hidden harmonic organization, though the framework remains exploratory.

title: Revisiting Cherenkov radiation in anisotropic chiral matter: exact calculation reveals threshold-free emission
comment: 31 pages, 12 figures. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D
summary: We explore Cherenkov radiation in anisotropic chiral matter within the framework of Carroll-Field-Jackiw electrodynamics, where the axion angle exhibits a linear dependence on position. By deriving closed-form expressions for the polarization modes of electromagnetic fields in cylindrical coordinates and the space-frequency domain, we solve the modified Maxwell's equations. To enforce causality, we impose outgoing wave boundary conditions at a cylindrical surface at infinity, which yields the dispersion relations. Our analysis uncovers the specific angles and frequency ranges that allow for zero, one, or two Cherenkov cones. We also obtain the spectral energy distribution of the radiation in all cases. Notably, one sector of the model exhibits a novel phenomenon: Cherenkov radiation can be generated by slowly moving charges without a threshold, but only within a specific frequency range. This behavior is not observed in standard materials. Using our exact calculations, we also investigate the reliability of an approximate method previously proposed based on the calculation of the Green's function for the system.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates Cherenkov radiation in anisotropic chiral matter using Carroll-Field-Jackiw electrodynamics with a position-dependent axion angle, deriving exact solutions for polarization modes, dispersion relations, and spectral energy distributions, and discovering a novel thresholdless Cherenkov radiation for slow charges within specific frequency ranges.

AI.method: The authors derive closed-form expressions for polarization modes in cylindrical coordinates and the space-frequency domain by solving modified Maxwell's equations in Carroll-Field-Jackiw electrodynamics with a linear position-dependent axion angle. Causality is enforced via outgoing wave boundary conditions at infinity to obtain dispersion relations.

title: Endpoint Logarithms in the NLO Mueller-Navelet Jet Vertex: Threshold Matching and BLM/MOM Prescription Sensitivity
summary: The endpoint region $ζ\to1$ of the NLO forward jet vertex has not been systematically separated from BFKL energy-scale terms in Mueller-Navelet phenomenology. Starting from the small-cone NLO vertex, we isolate the quark and gluon plus distributions and construct a BFKL-aware threshold matching scheme that preserves exact NLO accuracy. The conservative Scheme-II exponent resums only the ordinary endpoint logarithms and leaves the $χ(n,γ)\ln\bar N$ term in the fixed-order coefficient, avoiding an uncontrolled tower of mixed endpoint-BFKL logarithms. In fixed-baseline CMS tests, this matched vertex is a controlled deformation of an optimized-NLL pointwise BLM/MOM calculation: it moves $R_{21}=C_2/C_1$ in the high-$ΔY$ direction favored by CMS, but it does not improve $C_1/C_0$ or $R_{32}=C_3/C_2$ in the same prescription. A coefficient-projected table-BLM diagnostic improves the absolute moments but lowers $R_{21}$ and is sensitive to the large-$|ν|$ tail. Thus the endpoint matching is internally consistent and phenomenologically informative, while the present setup does not provide a simultaneous description of all five CMS azimuthal observables.

The scheme is internally consistent but does not simultaneously describe all five CMS azimuthal observables.

title: Multiplicity-dependent forward jet production in proton-nucleus collisions
summary: Forward jet production in proton--nucleus collisions probes a dilute projectile scattering from a dense small-$x$ nuclear gluon field, while the charged-particle multiplicity inside the jet probes the final-state cascade in the jet cone. We develop a factorization framework for single-inclusive forward jets with an internal multiplicity measurement by combining the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) description of the production process with soft-collinear effective theory (SCET) semi-inclusive jet functions. The construction preserves the inclusive limit exactly: at zero multiplicity weight it reduces to the known inclusive next-to-leading order (NLO)/resummed CGC forward-jet cross section. We define the multiplicity-measured jet operator in a CGC background, formulate the matching that separates PDF, BK/JIMWLK, Sudakov, SiJF, and multiplicity-evolution radiation, and identify the Wilson-line resolution mechanism through which saturation can modify the internal multiplicity evolution. The resulting framework shows that high-multiplicity forward jets are sensitive both to the quark/gluon mixture generated by the CGC production kernel and to finite-$Q_s$ corrections when an early in-cone splitting is resolved by the target. A baseline numerical implementation validates the factorized structure and illustrates the resulting multiplicity-conditioned nuclear modification.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a factorization framework combining CGC and SCET to study forward jet production with internal multiplicity measurements in proton-nucleus collisions, showing how saturation effects modify multiplicity evolution and nuclear modification.
AI.motivation: To understand how the dense nuclear gluon field (small-x saturation) affects both the production of forward jets and the internal charged-particle multiplicity distribution inside those jets in proton-nucleus collisions.
AI.method: Combines Color Glass Condensate (CGC) for the production process with soft-collinear effective theory (SCET) semi-inclusive jet functions; defines multiplicity-measured jet operators in CGC background; formulates matching separating PDF, BK/JIMWLK, Sudakov, SiJF, and multiplicity-evolution radiation; introduces Wilson-line resolution mechanism.

A baseline numerical implementation validates the factorized structure and shows multiplicity-conditioned nuclear modification.
AI.conclusion: The framework exactly recovers the inclusive NLO/resummed CGC forward-jet cross section at zero multiplicity weight, and demonstrates that saturation can modify internal multiplicity evolution through the Wilson-line resolution mechanism.

title: Matrix element method at NLO: A fine proof of concept in POWHEG
summary: The matrix element method (MEM) provides a fully probabilistic approach to confront experimental events with theory, retaining all correlations in the scattering matrix element. While leading-order MEM is widely used and automated, extending it to next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD is challenging due to infrared divergences, negative weights, extra final-state partons, and multi-dimensional phase-space integration. We demonstrate that the POWHEG method offers a practical path to MEM at NLO accuracy. By projecting real-emission events onto Born kinematics via the mappings inherited from the $\tilde{B} (Φ)$ function, our method consistently includes the hardest QCD radiation while preserving the NLO-accurate normalization. As a proof of concept, we apply it to fully leptonic $W^+ W^-$ production in the Standard Model (SM) effective field theory, focusing on a CP-even dimension-six triple-gauge-boson operator. Our NLO MEM implementation acts as a near-optimal classifier, exploiting spin- and polarization-dependent correlations among the final-state leptons to efficiently distinguish beyond-the-SM (BSM) from SM events. This demonstrates the potential of MEM at NLO for precision studies of electroweak processes and subtle BSM effects.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a practical method for extending the Matrix Element Method (MEM) to next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD using the POWHEG approach, and demonstrates its effectiveness as a near-optimal classifier for distinguishing BSM from SM events in W+W- production.
AI.motivation: The MEM at leading order is widely used and automated, but extending it to NLO in QCD is challenging due to infrared divergences, negative weights, extra final-state partons, and multi-dimensional phase-space integration. The authors aim to overcome these obstacles to enable NLO-accurate MEM.
AI.method: The method uses the POWHEG approach to project real-emission events onto Born kinematics via mappings inherited from the B̃(Φ) function, consistently including the hardest QCD radiation while preserving NLO-accurate normalization. The method is applied to fully leptonic W+W- production in the SMEFT, focusing on a CP-even dimension-six triple-gauge-boson operator.
AI.result: The NLO MEM implementation acts as a near-optimal classifier, exploiting spin- and polarization-dependent correlations among final-state leptons to efficiently distinguish BSM from SM events.
AI.conclusion: The work demonstrates the potential of MEM at NLO for precision studies of electroweak processes and subtle BSM effects.

title: DarkAgents
summary: We present DarkAgents: a multi-agent system that leverages the reasoning and code-generation capabilities of large language models (LLMs), together with deterministic tested human-written code, to build orchestrated pipelines for theoretical astroparticle physics research. While related approaches have been proposed in collider physics and cosmology, DarkAgents targets the specific challenges of this domain, such as model building, complex pipeline computations, multiple constraints and assumption auditing. The framework can be powered by different agentic command-line tools, including Mistral's, Anthropic's, OpenAI's and local LLMs via Ollama. As first implementation, we apply DarkAgents to the study of cosmological first order transitions, starting from a classically scale-invariant particle-physics model and ending with the fit to the NANOGrav nanohertz gravitational-waves spectrum. DarkAgent-PT provides as output i) the best-fit values of model parameters, ii) their existing experimental and observational constraints, iii) an audit report of the assumptions and priors entering both i) and ii), of particular relevance for astroparticle physics. Our test runs identify inconsistencies in some fits in the literature and produce novel ones based on the dissipative bulk-flow GW template. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/PhysicsZandi/DarkAgents.

AI.tldr: DarkAgents is a multi-agent system combining LLM reasoning/code-generation with human-written code for automated theoretical astroparticle physics research pipelines, demonstrated on cosmological first-order phase transitions and NANOGrav gravitational-wave spectrum fitting.
AI.motivation: To address the specific challenges of theoretical astroparticle physics (model building, complex pipeline computations, multiple constraints, assumption auditing) which are not sufficiently covered by existing multi-agent approaches in collider physics and cosmology.
AI.method: A multi-agent framework powered by LLMs (Mistral, Anthropic, OpenAI, local via Ollama) combined with deterministic human-written code; applied as DarkAgent-PT to study cosmological first-order transitions from a classically scale-invariant particle-physics model to NANOGrav spectrum fitting.
AI.result: Outputs best-fit model parameters, experimental/observational constraints, and an audit report of assumptions and priors; identified inconsistencies in existing literature fits and produced novel fits using the dissipative bulk-flow gravitational-wave template.
AI.conclusion: The system demonstrates that LLM-driven multi-agent pipelines can effectively automate and audit complex astroparticle physics analyses, uncovering literature inconsistencies and generating new results.

title: MATCHA: A Mathematica package for matching UV models onto HEFT
summary: We present MATChing HEFT Amplitudes (MATCHA), a Mathematica package designed for leading-order (LO) matching of an ultraviolet (UV) model to the Higgs Effective Field Theory (HEFT). MATCHA performs the matching of non-decoupling effects $\mathcal{O}(1)$ to the LO HEFT lagrangian for an arbitrary number of Higgs fields. The main benefit of \heftmatcha is that it is built on existing packages such as \texttt{FeynArts} and \texttt{FormCalc}, which are familiar to the user, and directly benefits from the established features of these packages. In addition, \heftmatcha is designed to require minimal input from the user, requiring solely the \texttt{FeynRules} output files and the desired order of expansion. In this way, \heftmatcha provides the leading low-energy couplings capturing non-decoupling effects of HEFT.

AI.tldr: MATCHA is a Mathematica package for matching UV models to the Higgs Effective Field Theory (HEFT) at leading order, computing non-decoupling effects with minimal user input via integration with FeynArts, FormCalc, and FeynRules.
AI.motivation: To provide an automated, user-friendly tool for matching UV models to HEFT, capturing non-decoupling effects at leading order, built on familiar existing packages to minimize user effort.
AI.method: MATCHA leverages FeynArts, FormCalc, and FeynRules to perform LO matching of non-decoupling effects O(1) to the HEFT Lagrangian, requiring only FeynRules output files and the desired expansion order as input.
AI.result: A Mathematica package that computes leading low-energy couplings capturing non-decoupling effects of HEFT for an arbitrary number of Higgs fields with minimal user input.
AI.conclusion: MATCHA offers an efficient, accessible tool for HEFT matching that builds on well-established packages, reducing the barrier for users to compute non-decoupling effects in UV-to-HEFT matching.
